4cc0b874c51572d1c68a46add9f5991c62487431.title: Backend: validation, rate limit, cache, GitHub client, all API routes
4cc0b874c51572d1c68a46add9f5991c62487431.whatChanged: Added five new source files implementing the backend layer: cache read/write against a database table, a GitHub API client that fetches repo metadata, file trees, file contents, and commits, HTTP request handlers for chat review, repo overview, commit listing, commit explanation, and project kickoff, plus input validation and rate-limit usage. The diff shows new files only, with no deletions.
4cc0b874c51572d1c68a46add9f5991c62487431.whyItMatters: This commit creates the complete backend surface of the app: it lets the frontend call defined API routes, protects against bad input with validation, limits LLM spending with rate limiting, avoids repeated GitHub and LLM calls with caching, and isolates private chat/idea data from the public repo cache.
4cc0b874c51572d1c68a46add9f5991c62487431.designReasoning: Separation of concerns: cache, GitHub client, handlers, validation, rate limiting, LLM calls, and prompts live in separate files. The GitHub client is the only place that calls fetch to github.com, centralizing auth headers, timeouts, and error mapping. Handlers validate input before any work, cache public repo results keyed by repo and head SHA, skip caching for private chats and ideas, and ground LLM outputs by filtering module evidence to paths that actually exist in the fetched file tree.
4cc0b874c51572d1c68a46add9f5991c62487431.tradeoffs: Caching public repo analyses by head SHA means results are stale until the repo is pushed to again; the commit accepts this to avoid repeated GitHub API and LLM calls. Truncating file trees to 350 listed files and key-file contents to 3000 chars bounds LLM input size and cost but may miss relevant files. Filtering out modules without existing evidence paths improves accuracy but can drop legitimate modules if path matching fails.
alternatives: Use an in-memory cache instead of the database-backed cache, which would lose data on restart but avoid database latency.
Call GitHub directly from each handler instead of a centralized client, which would duplicate auth, timeout, and error-handling code.
Cache chat and kickoff results too, which would improve speed but risks storing private user data in the shared cache table.
Return raw GitHub responses instead of transformed RepoMeta and CommitSummary types, which would simplify the client but push API-shape knowledge into handlers.

evidence.hint: getCached and putCached read/write rows from the analyses table using cache_key, payload, and created_at columns.
gh helper fetches https://api.github.com with Bearer auth, 10-second timeout, and maps 404/403/429 to HttpError; getMeta, getTree, getFile, listCommits, getCommit wrap GitHub endpoints.

reviewChat, overview, commits, explainCommit, kickoffHandler map to POST /api/chat/review, GET /api/repo/overview, GET /api/repo/commits, POST /api/commit/explain, POST /api/kickoff; readBody with zod schemas validates input; spendLlmCall enforces rate limits; getCached/putCached store public results only.

b698ba3c6134bbe3f018ca63190c324318c51582.title: LLM Feasibility Results
b698ba3c6134bbe3f018ca63190c324318c51582.whatChanged: The code now includes LLM feasibility results, a chosen model, and a verified fallback.
b698ba3c6134bbe3f018ca63190c324318c51582.whyItMatters: This change matters because it allows for the integration of LLM models into the system, enabling features like automated commit explanations.
b698ba3c6134bbe3f018ca63190c324318c51582.designReasoning: The design reasoning behind this change is to use LLM models to generate commit explanations, with a focus on selecting a suitable model and handling potential errors or inconsistencies in the model output.
b698ba3c6134bbe3f018ca63190c324318c51582.tradeoffs: The tradeoffs of this change include the potential for model output to be inconsistent or inaccurate, as well as the need to handle errors and exceptions when working with the LLM models.
alternatives: Implementing a custom commit explanation system

69e3c3c8366add4fa43c271ac95dbac1db4358f6.title: Step 1 prep: LLM layer, prompts, feasibility harness, zod
69e3c3c8366add4fa43c271ac95dbac1db4358f6.whatChanged: Added an LLM integration layer in src/llm.ts that calls NVIDIA NIM and Cloudflare Workers AI, parses JSON output, and retries between providers. Added prompt builders in src/prompts/chatReview.ts and src/prompts/commitExplain.ts with Zod schemas for structured responses. Added shared constants in src/prompts/common.ts. Added a feasibility harness in scripts/llm-test.ts and sample chats in scripts/samples.ts. Added zod dependency in package.json, scripts/out to .gitignore, and allowImportingTsExtensions in tsconfig.json.
69e3c3c8366add4fa43c271ac95dbac1db4358f6.whyItMatters: This prepares the system to automatically review AI chats and explain git commits using structured LLM output, which makes results predictable and testable before wider rollout.
69e3c3c8366add4fa43c271ac95dbac1db4358f6.designReasoning: The code separates concerns by putting provider logic in src/llm.ts, prompt templates in src/prompts/, and shared concept lists in src/prompts/common.ts. It uses Zod schemas to validate model JSON output, ensuring the response matches the expected shape. It falls back from NIM to Workers AI if the first provider fails, improving reliability.
69e3c3c8366add4fa43c271ac95dbac1db4358f6.tradeoffs: Hardcoding the NVIDIA API URL and fallback model reduces flexibility but keeps the initial implementation simple. Catching all errors silently in the retry loop hides which provider failed, making debugging harder. Reading .dev.vars manually couples the harness to local file-based secrets instead of using environment bindings directly.
alternatives: Use a single LLM provider instead of retrying across two
Use environment variables directly instead of parsing .dev.vars
Use a dedicated LLM client library instead of raw fetch

902be1564b6ac30f7e7982b2e96adafbdb86526e.title: Bind D1 database and rename worker to lumen-learn for deploy
902be1564b6ac30f7e7982b2e96adafbdb86526e.whatChanged: Renamed the project from "lumen" to "lumen-learn" in package.json and wrangler.jsonc, and replaced the placeholder D1 database ID with a real UUID so the worker can connect to its database.
902be1564b6ac30f7e7982b2e96adafbdb86526e.whyItMatters: The worker can now deploy with a real database binding instead of a placeholder, and the deployment name matches the project name.
902be1564b6ac30f7e7982b2e96adafbdb86526e.designReasoning: Cloudflare Workers use wrangler.jsonc to declare resources; the database binding named DB lets code in src/index.ts access the D1 database at runtime.
902be1564b6ac30f7e7982b2e96adafbdb86526e.tradeoffs: Hardcoding a real database ID ties this repository to one specific database, making it less portable across environments than using a placeholder or environment variable.
alternatives: Use environment variables for the database ID
Keep separate wrangler config files per environment
